<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by keeping the motion’s real choice—class-wide digitization and funded access versus a locatable right to the claimant’s own file—from being collapsed. A’s duty-of-repair and “erased cannot petition” case stayed live and morally sharp, but A never resolved the tension between honoring refusals and digitizing kinship networks. B’s non-compulsion answer showed only the state program can override a birth parent’s or nation’s “no,” giving the cleaner reason to reject the proposition as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2: a firm cannot legislate sealed files open, and a fee-waived locator for the file that names the claimant is not publicly funded access to the class.</best_rebuttal>
